Notes: Earliest documented presence: in the 1840s a plot on the right bank of the Oka was allotted for a Jewish cemetery (year = midpoint of 1840s)
Community originated in the mid-19th century when a small number of retired 'Nicholas soldiers' settled permanently in Orel (year = approx. midpoint of 'mid-19th century')
Jews living in Orel in 1867
Archival file: petition of Jewish craftsmen of the city of Orel for permission to open a prayer school (1874); organized presence, no count
First Jewish prayer house opened in 1876 on Moskovskaya Street; the religious community then numbered about 200 people (congregation subset; not total population)
Small Jewish community founded in 2nd half of 19th century; in 1876 authorized to build a synagogue
Over 500 Jews in Orel in 1880 ('svyshe 500')
Community states it has existed since 1880; organized community, no count
Jewish cemetery enlarged 'in connection with growth of Jewish residents'; no count
1897 census: 1,750 Jews (2.5% of total population)
Anti-Jewish riots on Oct. 18, 1905; many injured and shops looted
Mikveh built in 1905
New synagogue built 1909-1911, officially opened 1912 (144 seats)
During World War I many refugees from the battle areas came to the town (year = approximate midpoint of WWI; no count)
Pogrom by units of the Volunteer (White) Army in 1919
1923: 3,739 Jews; synagogue closed spring 1923
Soviet authorities closed the synagogue in spring 1923
1926 census: 3,597 Jews (4.6% of total)
1939 census: 3,143 Jews (2.84% of total)
'More than 7,000 Jews' lived in the city before WWII per community site; conflicts with 1939 census (3,143) - may include refugees 1939-41; most evacuated east
Germans occupied the city Oct 3, 1941; ghetto created November 1941 (no resident count given)
Ghetto liquidated Sept 3, 1942: 175 Jews shot (death toll, not population)
Most remaining Jews killed Aug-Dec 1942; the last murdered Feb-July 1943
Synagogue opened in 1945 after liberation (1943)
Jewish religious community re-established in 1992
Jewish religious organization 'Tsentr Shalom' founded Sept 13, 1999, joined FEOR
2002 census: 511 Jews
2010 census: Jews 0.1% of city population (no absolute count given)
Synagogue building returned to the Orel Jewish religious community on Nov 21, 2016
